The furnace of Command Level One remains a crushing, pressurized weight. Helena does not hesitate to calculate the cost. Her fingers fly across her command console interface, rerouting power matrices and recalibrating frequency modulators at blinding speed. She recognizes this maneuver as a tactical gamble of staggering magnitude—a deliberate introduction of logical flaw into an optimized system.

"Injecting a chaotic waveform," Helena confirms, her voice low but steady. "This will destabilize the field's harmonic equilibrium immediately. Expect high-energy feedback."

The EMDF field responds instantly to the discordant input. The strained indigo containment barrier around Sector One doesn’t simply waver—it begins to *shimmer*, its stable geometry collapsing into a flickering, agitated pattern that looks like liquid data under pressure.

The rhythmic pulsing stops dead, replaced by a high-frequency shudder that rattles the station hull and sends a spike of intense thermal energy into the command level.

The Entity is rejecting the noise. The dissonance has triggered an immediate, catastrophic countermeasure in its informational core. Jora Ward stiffens against the breach point; the structural groan of the station becomes a sharp, deafening *screech* as the assimilated architecture violently tries to self-correct and reassert dominance over the newly introduced chaos.

"The only way to force informational disruption without guaranteeing immediate kinetic overload," Jora advises, her tone hardening with professional rigor, "is via a targeted energy signature—not just frequency change. It needs to be an external pulse delivered through the containment field's *input*."
